A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRISM and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their retained material can be matched reliably despite substantial rewriting and internal inconsistencies in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments, training-throughput measurements, component ablations, and nine synthetic probing tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds language-model perplexity, zero-shot benchmark results, and language-model ablations in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The core architecture and recurrent update remain recognizable. However, v3 Equation 8 and Figure 1 change initialization from r=v-u to r=v, while Algorithm 1 still specifies V-U. Its new Gated DeltaNet base-case descriptions also conflict over L=0 versus L=1. These inconsistencies prevent reliably distinguishing an actual procedural revision from documentation errors.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds language modeling on SlimPajama and zero-shot evaluation including WikiText, LAMBADA, PIQA, ARC, BoolQ, and other benchmarks. This substantially expands coverage beyond the four recommendation datasets and nine synthetic probes retained from v1.

E2.justification: The recommendation and synthetic-probing comparator sets are unchanged. The new language-model comparisons add evaluated EFLA and PGDN baselines, alongside Gated DeltaNet and Mamba-2, which were already evaluated elsewhere in v1.

E3.justification: The new language-model experiments introduce approximately 130M-parameter models trained on 2B tokens, validation/test perplexity, and zero-shot evaluation. Separately, Section 5.1 revises the stated recommendation cutoffs from K=10 to K={100,200,500}, although both versions' tables already report 200/500. Table 3 relabels the unchanged single-step ablation scores from L=1 to L=0; a rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix I.4 adds a substantial mechanism study comparing independent directions, shared keys, reuse of the GDN base key, removal of residual subtraction, and a single solver step. These test the contributions of direction diversity and iterative refinement to language-model generalization. The original recommendation ablation scores and synthetic probing results are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added language-model tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 7-9 add perplexity, downstream accuracy, and ablation results; for example, final test perplexity is 23.13 for PRISM versus 23.28 for GDN. Numerical entries in the original recommendation, component-ablation, and synthetic-probing tables are unchanged. The new Table 8 averages are internally inconsistent with its displayed task accuracies, limiting interpretation of the reported aggregate gains.

T1.justification: Section 3 introduces a unified proximal-plus-nonlinear-retrieval objective. New Appendix B derives the TTT-MLP correspondence and shows that repeated updates with a fixed key remain rank one, motivating independently learned directions. It also adds GDN special-case arguments. The earlier degeneracy, spectral, proxy-error, and stability analyses largely remain in condensed, relocated form.

C1.justification: The contributions shift from solver-inspired residual fitting toward a unified OCP framework, explicitly claiming a shared objective with TTT/GDN, the first Rank-L/parallel-scan combination, and backward compatibility with GDN. These strengthen the claimed theoretical relationship to existing methods. The central Rank-L expressivity and 174-fold throughput claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly interprets the language-model results as favoring Rank-L injection over exact flow/preconditioning and residual iteration over direction multiplicity for generalization. Existing limitations concerning local proxies and fixed memory capacity remain. Some new interpretation overreaches: the claim that every ablation worsens perplexity conflicts with shared-key LAMBADA perplexity improving from 27.00 to 26.02.

D1.justification: v3 adds the SlimPajama token budget, tokenizer, parameter counts, and language-model configurations, and changes the supplied repository link. However, it removes v1's recommendation data provenance, item-frequency filtering threshold, and chronological leave-one-out instructions. It also omits the synthetic experiments' 10k-step budget and MoM four-expert configuration. These are substantive changes in reproducibility information, without establishing corresponding experimental changes.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around OCP and a Rank-Parallel taxonomy, positioning PRISM as an amortized counterpart to TTT and a generalization of GDN. PGDN and Su's stability discussion are added, while the RetNet reference is removed. EFLA moves from cited background to an evaluated comparator.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, theoretical motivation, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Appendices are reorganized and proofs substantially compressed. The restructuring also leaves duplicated baseline sections and a repeated computational-complexity paragraph.

P2.justification: Table 1 is rebuilt around mathematical objectives, and recommendation tables are regrouped by rank and parallelism. v3 adds a structural-correspondence table and three language-model tables, updates and relocates Figure 1, and relocates Figure 2. Dataset statistics are displayed twice in Tables 10 and 13.

improvement.justification: Appendix I adds valuable evidence beyond recommendation and useful mechanism ablations. However, v3 introduces conflicting algorithm descriptions and unreliable aggregate reporting: Table 8's nine PRISM accuracies average approximately 41.19%, rather than the reported 40.1%. It also drops important preprocessing, split, and training details retained in v1. The broader evidence and explanatory additions coexist with losses in consistency and reproducibility, preventing a confident judgment of net improvement.
